result.decision_rationale: The focused gate passed on the submitted commit, and the five pending findings are fixed for their reported cases. Five additional source-level defects remain in toolbar placement and lifecycle handling. They can move or resurrect a shortcut, make a continuing game disagree with its save, or retain a disposed player world while the mod is disabled.

required_gaps: Correct the five toolbar and lifecycle paths below, exercise their distinguishing sequences, and obtain a focused receipt on the corrected candidate.

findings.actual: The canonical emptying branch records interrupted intent and increments NativeSlotInvalidationCount, but leaves placementRecorded unset. ResolveUnbound correctly gives up the occupied slot. TryInitialPlacement then sees an unrecorded rider and places the shortcut in another empty main-bar slot when autofill is enabled. The outgoing-load copy of canonical invalidation also omits the placement record.
findings.blocking_rationale: A first manual placement can turn into an unsolicited shortcut elsewhere after the player gives its slot to another ability.
findings.expected: Observing the player's canonical shortcut satisfies one-time placement even when native UI empties it. If its chosen slot becomes occupied, the shortcut stays off the bar.
findings.requested_correction: Record successful canonical invalidation in the one-time placement set belonging to the same world. Apply the same rule to the outgoing records restored after an abandoned load.
findings.requested_evidence: Extend the existing first-manual-placement cleanup case. Put an ordinary ability in the emptied slot before recovery, enable autofill, and verify it stays there with no Mount / Dismount shortcut elsewhere through update, save and reload.
findings.title: Native emptying of a first manual shortcut leaves autofill armed
findings.trigger: Native UI empties a manually placed canonical shortcut before the first regular observation. Its chosen slot is filled before the same pet's control returns.

findings.actual: LegacyAliasIndex reads the bar after earlier slots may already have been emptied. If cleanup empties a canonical binding at 4 and then an old Mount alias at 9, the second observation sees 9 as the chosen alias. Applying the pending reports first remembers 4, then ObserveNativeAliasInvalidated overwrites it with 9. The existing mixed-bar control cleans the alias while the canonical slot is still present, so it misses this order.
findings.blocking_rationale: An older supported bar restores the shortcut to a different index depending on native cleanup order.
findings.expected: The canonical slot wins over an older alias on the same bar, including when native cleanup empties both during one pass.
findings.requested_correction: Preserve the selected public binding for the cleanup operation before its slot mutations can change precedence. Ensure a later report for a secondary binding cannot replace that choice.
findings.requested_evidence: Run a cleanup pass over a stale canonical at 4 and a stale alias at 9 with neither fact live. After both slots empty, require one saved and restored public binding at 4. Retain the alias-only recovery control.
findings.title: A later legacy alias can override the canonical slot during native cleanup
findings.trigger: A mixed legacy bar loses both public bindings during temporary unavailability, with native cleanup visiting the canonical slot first.

findings.actual: CaptureAbsentIntent passes occupancy to AbsentRowsAfterLive, which emits a placement record alone. The in-memory entry still contains the interrupted index. While the pet remains unavailable, reconciliation keeps that index. If the player clears the occupant before the pet returns, the continuing game restores the shortcut there. Reloading the save first leaves it off the bar.
findings.blocking_rationale: Continuing after a save and reloading that same save produce different arrangements after the same toolbar edit.
findings.expected: Once the save boundary observes a different ability in the remembered slot and classifies the shortcut as off the bar, that decision also governs the continuing game.
findings.requested_correction: Apply the occupied-slot decision to the rider's current placement intent as well as its emitted rows. Preserve the occupant and the one-time placement record.
findings.requested_evidence: With the same pet temporarily unavailable and an ordinary ability occupying remembered slot 9, save. Compare continuing against reloading that save. In each case remove the occupant before the pet returns and require the shortcut to remain off the bar.
findings.title: An occupied slot is given up in the archive but retained in memory
findings.trigger: A player saves while another ability occupies an interrupted shortcut's index, then clears that ability while the pet is still unavailable.

findings.actual: WrapLoadRoutine calls BeginSelectedLoad while controls are disabled. The fence takes a strong reference to the outgoing Player. On successful replacement, Update returns at !enabled before reaching ArrangementsAccepted, and the successful load path does not release the fence. A disabled session without a later toolbar operation can therefore retain the previous player graph. The installed IsBad observer also accepts new placement observations while disabled because its entry guard checks only disposal and registration.
findings.blocking_rationale: Disabling the mod clears its records once, but a subsequent ordinary load can recreate toolbar state and keep a disposed world reachable.
findings.expected: A disabled control service releases the outgoing player on world replacement and does not acquire placement intent from native toolbar cleanup.
findings.requested_correction: Make load-fence ownership and toolbar observations respect the disabled lifecycle. Preserve save sanitation and the enabled service's abandoned-load recovery.
findings.requested_evidence: Disable KMC, complete a load from player A to player B, and verify the toolbar service releases A without re-enable or another save. Exercise native cleanup on a surviving legacy slot while disabled and verify it creates no placement record.
findings.title: A load while KMC is disabled can retain the outgoing player
findings.trigger: The owner disables KMC in a loaded game, loads another save and continues playing with KMC disabled.

findings.actual: ApplySlotInvalidation returns immediately for a successful rebind while the outgoing world is fenced. If its saved intent was interrupted, abandoning the load restores that interrupted entry even though native cleanup made the shortcut live again. A removal before the next update is then treated as recoverable and the shortcut comes back.
findings.blocking_rationale: Canceling a load can reverse a deliberate removal of a repaired shortcut in the surviving world.
findings.expected: A successful rebind updates the outgoing world's saved arrangement to live. An abandoned load returns that state, and a completed replacement discards it.
findings.requested_correction: Apply the rebind outcome to the owning fence's outgoing intent and placement record while keeping the incoming world's records isolated.
findings.requested_evidence: Begin a load with interrupted intent and a stale canonical slot at 9. Rebind it during fenced cleanup, abandon the load, then remove the repaired shortcut before reconciliation. Require a record-only save and an empty slot after reload. Keep completed replacement as the isolation control.
findings.title: An abandoned load discards a native rebind observed in the surviving world
findings.trigger: Native cleanup repairs a previously interrupted slot while a selected load fences the outgoing player, and the load is abandoned.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: Production now classifies the resulting slot by KMC kind and live fact data. The focused assembly check inspects the pinned cleanup method's construction and field store, and the regression drives rebind and empty outcomes through the production classifier.

For the reported single returned alias, successful invalidation marks its recorded placement interrupted. The update-first and save-first cases recover one shortcut at 9. R14-F2 concerns a second binding in the same cleanup pass.

Save-boundary observation now records a visible manual placement, and TryInitialPlacement yields to its pending public-slot lease. The regression checks one shortcut at 9 after release, subsequent updates and reload.

The remembered-row writer checks both the occupant and emitted indices. The codec case preserves the Charge row and one placement record, and still rejects an injected duplicate. R14-F3 concerns the continuing in-memory arrangement after that valid save.

Each deferred report carries its originating player. The mutation of placement state now requires that player and the exact reporting unit on its roster before the load fence can release. The regression covers replacement and abandonment.

The focused gate passed. Toolbar intent and cleanup still need the corrections listed above.
